State machines for permission checking, queue overflow recovery, and display mode activation are not shown.
Callable entry points, system call numbers, and function signatures beyond ioctl numbers are not shown.

findings.text: File access hints use small integers where the hint meaning drop unneeded pages has value four and the hint meaning data is used once has value five.

File range manipulation flags are single bit values where allocate range is zero, keep size is one, punch hole is two, no hide stale is four, collapse range is eight, zero range is sixteen, insert range is thirty two, unshare range is sixty four, and write zeroes is one hundred twenty eight.

Filesystem notification event bits occupy low mask positions with distinct powers of two for access, modify, attribute change, writable close, unwritable close, open, moved from, moved to, create, delete, self delete, self move, and execution open, progressing from bit zero through bit twelve with a gap before overflow and error bits.

Higher notification mask positions distinguish queue overflow, filesystem error, open permission check, access permission check, execute permission check, pre access hook, mount attach, mount detach, interest in child events, rename, and directory targeting, each assigned a separate single bit.

Initialization behavior selects one notification class among zero, four, and eight, plus independent option bits for close on exec, nonblocking operation, unlimited queue, unlimited marks, and audit enable; the defined aggregates combine all class bits and the main init subset respectively.

Event reporting modifiers request alternate process identification, thread identity, file identifier, directory identifier, name data, target identifier, file descriptor error reporting, and mount information, with defined combinations joining directory identifier with name and further adding file and target identifiers.

Mark control uses separate bits for add, remove, do not follow links, only directories, ignored mask handling, ignored survival across modify, flush, evictable, and ignore, while mark scope selects inode, mount, filesystem, or mount namespace targets with fixed encodings including zero for inode.

Event mask aggregates group writable and unwritable closes into close, both move directions into move, access plus modify plus close plus open into all events, open permission plus access permission into all permission events, and all events plus all permission events plus overflow into all outgoing events.
Every notification record carries the same metadata version number three, so consumers can reject records with a different version as incompatible.

A notification record contains a total record length, a version octet, a reserved octet, a fixed header length, an aligned wide event mask, a descriptor for the affected object, and a process identifier, in that logical order.

Variable length extra information after a notification is typed by small integers where file identifier is one, directory identifier plus name is two, plain directory identifier is three, process descriptor is four, error is five, range is six, mount is seven, old directory name is ten, and new directory name is twelve.

Each extra information item starts with a common header of type, padding, and length; specializations then add filesystem identity plus a trailing variable handle, or a process descriptor, or an error code plus repeat count, or padding plus offset plus byte count, or a mount identifier.

A permission answer contains an object descriptor and a decision word; optional attached answer data uses a small typed header, with the audit rule form adding rule number and subject and object trust values.

Permission answers distinguish allow with value one and deny with value two, reserve zero and one for response information kinds meaning none and audit rule, and reserve negative one for missing descriptor or process descriptor plus negative two for an expired process descriptor.

Deny answers can embed an eight bit error number in the high octet of the decision word while audit request and extra information presence are signaled by separate low bits, so decoding must mask and shift rather than compare for equality.

Consumers iterate a byte buffer by using each record stored length to advance and shrink the remaining count, and treat a record as usable only when remaining bytes cover at least one fixed header and the stored length is within header size and remaining bytes.

Framebuffer support allows up to thirty two devices and exposes numeric control operations for variable and fixed information, colormap access, panning, console mapping, blanking, vertical blank retrieval, allocation, glyph and hardware information, mode and display information, cursor, and vertical sync wait.

Framebuffer organization distinguishes packed pixels, planes, interleaved planes, text, VGA planes, and FOURCC identified formats, with separate small enumerations for text auxiliaries, VGA plane auxiliaries, monochrome and color visuals including FOURCC, plus a wide accelerator identifier table and a capability bit for FOURCC formats.

Fixed display information carries an identification string, physical start and length for pixel memory and for mapped control registers, type and auxiliary codes, visual code, panning and wrapping steps, bytes per line, accelerator identity, capability flags, and reserved space for future growth.

A color component descriptor carries start position, width, and a flag for reversed most significant bit placement; related activation policy distinguishes immediate, next open, test only, and a mask, while nonstandard modes flag hold and modify and reversed pixel order in a byte.

These headers publish user visible numeric interfaces and record layouts for file hints, file range operations, filesystem event monitoring and permission responses, and framebuffer control, guarded by their respective include sentinels.
